206974007.description:
Devyn is a breathtakingly beautiful black cat with a glossy midnight coat and striking eyes that reflect every bit of her intelligence and curiosity. At just 2 years old, she already carries herself with the elegance and quiet confidence of a feline queen.

Curious by nature, Devyn loves to explore her surroundings and observe from a safe, elevated spot. She’s fascinated by the world around her, but she prefers to approach everything-especially people-in her own time. Devyn has some trust issues and can be cautious with new humans, but she’s making steady progress. Her foster mom is gently earning her trust day by day, and Devyn is showing more and more of her sweet, inquisitive personality.

Devyn isn’t shy about expressing her feelings. She is very vocal when she’s unhappy or uncomfortable, making her a cat who communicates clearly and honestly. Her ideal home is one where her boundaries are respected and her cues are understood.

She does get along well with both dogs and other cats, as long as they respect her space and don’t overwhelm her. Calm, patient companions-furry or human-will help her shine.

Devyn is looking for someone who sees the beauty in letting a relationship unfold naturally. With patience, understanding, and love, she’ll reward you with trust, companionship, and her own special brand of charm.

211913939.description:
Hi, I’m Pepper! 🐾

I’m an 8 ½ year-old bundle of love with the biggest heart and so much love to give! My foster family says I’m a special girl with a goofy personality, a playful spirit, and a heart that is truly one of a kind.

I may need a little extra patience and understanding when getting to know new people and navigating the world around me. New experiences and unfamiliar dogs can sometimes feel overwhelming, so I’m looking for someone who understands that building trust is a process. I may not open my heart overnight, but when I do, you’ll have a friend who loves with her whole heart. Once I trust you, you’ll get to see the real Pepper - the silly, affectionate, playful girl who loves to snuggle, give kisses, lean in for affection, and make you laugh. I have so much personality packed into this big body, and I truly believe I’m a lap dog! My favorite things include toys, treats, naps, and spending time with my people. And yes, my adorable snoring is just one of my many charms!

I currently live with another female dog, and we have a wonderful relationship. We love to play and chase each other, and she is a very special part of my world. While I do well with my resident dog, I have found that I’m most comfortable in a home where I don’t have to share my people or space with other dogs. I would likely thrive as the only dog in the home, where I can soak up all the love and attention. I’m looking for a quieter home with a patient, compassionate person or family who understands my needs and will give me the time and support I deserve. A female-led home would be a wonderful fit for me, and I would do best without children. I’m hoping for someone who sees the beauty in taking things slowly and understands that the most meaningful relationships are built one day at a time.

My foster family has watched me come so far. I’m learning that the world can be a wonderful place and that new experiences don’t always have to be scary. Every little bit of progress makes us so proud, and we know there is still so much happiness ahead of me. I’m a playful, loving girl who has so much more to discover. I may need someone willing to be patient, but I promise that the love I give in return is worth every moment. Once you become my person, you’ll have a loyal companion who wants nothing more than to be by your side. My foster family loves me dearly, and while saying goodbye will be incredibly difficult, they know there is someone out there who will see just how extraordinary I am.

I’m not looking for a perfect home. I’m looking for the right home - a home with patience, understanding, and a whole lot of heart. If you’re willing to give me the time I need to feel safe and loved, I’ll show you just how much love this big-hearted girl has to give ❤️

Maple is great with other dogs and she will need another dog in the home to help her adjust and feel comfortable. She is also great with cats. She does play with them as our cats enjoy playing with her.

She does well with kids, but would be best in a home without young kids, due to her tending to be more on the skiddish side, as well as her jumping.

Maple is a high energy pup who needs a fenced in yard to safely get her frequent zoomies out. She does pretty well on a leash, but she won't potty while she is leashed.

She loves to play with leaves and recently discovered that she thoroughly enjoys the pool and the hose. Watching her enjoy the simple things brings so much joy and laughter everyday.

While she definitely has her stubborn tendencies and little quirks, I know there is a perfect family for her out there that will love her just the way she is.

212449123.description:
Meet Jillian (a.k.a. Junie)!

If you are looking for a pup with a ton of personality and a lot of love, then Jillian is your girl.

With big amber eyes and a uniquely painted coat, Jillian is a little showstopper. She loves all humans she meets and is a huge sweetheart, but does need continued boundary work as she thinks the best way to let others know she is a fan is to get right up into their personal space! While she is smart and has picked up on cues and commands very quickly, ongoing training is still needed.

Jillian is now crate trained and has done well being crated for longer periods of time while her foster is at work. When crated, she tends to do better in a high-traffic area so she can observe what is going on around her and not miss out. The only time she cries anymore when crated is because she has a serious case of FOMO and just wants to join in the fun. While Jillian has not been left alone in the house outside the crate for long periods of time, during shorter bouts, she has done really well and usually just ends up lounging in the living room or sunroom.

Jillian is potty-trained and does very well with potty prompts once outside. She did clear our 3-foot fence at one point and had a nice little run in our neighbor’s yard so is currently on a lead even with a fenced-in backyard. As an almost 2-year-old, Jillian still has a lot of youthful energy and looks forward to going for her walk first thing in the morning. And while she has made a lot of progress over the last few months, Jillian does have a high prey drive and exhibits some excitable reactivity as a result.

Jillian is normally taken on a couple walks a day to work on her leash skills and she is catching on really quickly - we are learning to “leave it”, “wait”, and “eyes” (when needing her attention); she tends to crowd and pull on the leash so we are also working on side-by-side walking and pressure commands with the leash. She also still struggles with off-leash recall but with continued patience and consistency, will no doubt continue to improve. Overall, she would greatly benefit from working with a trainer as it appears that most things are still very new to her.

While Jillian initially did well with the resident dog, more recently, she seems to be struggling to read different social cues and has shown some aggressive reactivity. As a result, we have been keeping her on a lead or in the crate as a precaution when both dogs are in a shared space in the house. Since Jillian was found as a stray, it is hard to know her history with other dogs; she does express high interest in playing with other dogs but will require high levels of monitoring.

In just a short amount of time, Jillian has learned both the verbal and nonverbal signals for “sit”, “wait”, “hands in”, “stay” and “lie down”. She transports well and loves her weekly outdoor adventures at Fort Snelling. Overall, Jillian's ideal home is with an active family or person who is patient, does not have any other pets, is in a house (she does have a heavy bark!) with a high fenced-in yard. If you are ready for a lively spirit, funny personality, and unconditional companionship - look no further than Jillian!

Meet Buttercup!

Buttercup is a sweet, gentle pup who can be a little shy and reserved when meeting new people, but once she feels safe she becomes very loving and loyal to her people.

Buttercup has low-to-moderate energy and enjoys both playtime and cuddles. She loves playing fetch and will happily bring the ball back so you can throw it again. She’s also extremely treat and food motivated, which makes training fun and rewarding. Belly rubs, snacks, and greeting her people when they come home are some of her favorite things.

She is good with other dogs, but can be reactive when she sees them from a distance and does best with slow introductions. Buttercup doesn’t need another dog in the home, but a calm, friendly dog could help build her confidence.

Buttercup is afraid of men and will need a patient home that allows her time to warm up. Because she isn’t familiar with toddlers, she would do best with older children. She sleeps well in her crate at night and learned potty training quickly.

Buttercup cannot live with cats.

She’s a very sweet, cuddly girl who has clearly had a difficult past and just needs a patient family who will give her the love and security she deserves.

From my foster mom: Chat GPT estimates that he will be around 50 lbs fully grown, so if you are looking for a pup with the looks of a big dog, but on the smaller side, Norman is for you! I think he would do best in a home with another dog! Both for his happiness, and to allow him to burn some of his boundless energy off easily. He has lived with small children before, and his energy level and love for play chomping did not work out well. He is very sweet and gentle with children when meeting them, but it may be best for him to go to a home with older children only. I am hoping he grows out of some of that, but only time will tell! Shalla has spent much of her life being a devoted mama, and now it’s her turn to be cared for. And care for her you will—because she is stunning. From her beautifully lined eyes to her glowing golden coat, she turns heads wherever she goes.

We aren’t quite sure of her breed, but she has the majestic face of a wolf paired with big, elegant paws—though she’s not especially tall. Her coat is thick, sleek, and surprisingly easy to maintain considering how full it is.

Shalla would thrive in a home with people around most of the time. She loves kids and enjoys being part of the action. She’s polite with other dogs—she likes them well enough but doesn’t necessarily need a canine companion to be happy. What she does need is togetherness. Shalla doesn’t love being alone, and adopters should be prepared to use a heavy‑duty crate and possibly medication when away from home.

Aside from that, she is an amazing, well‑behaved dog who simply wants to be close to her people. And yes—we know you’re wondering—she has had zero accidents.

If you’re looking for a loyal, affectionate companion who will soak up every moment by your side, Shalla is ready to finally be someone’s “baby.”

213539678.description:
Wilde & Lightfoot – Bonded Brothers Looking for a Patient Forever Home

Sometimes two is better than one, and that is definitely the case with these bonded brothers!

When Wilde and Lightfoot first came into rescue, they were very stressed and unsure of the world around them. Since then, they have been slowly learning to trust humans and discovering just how wonderful love and affection can be. Wilde is the more confident of the pair and helps show his brother, Lightfoot, that people can be safe and kind.

Once they feel comfortable, both boys enjoy pets and attention. Lightfoot has even been known to give sweet little kisses! Their bond is truly special—when they once thought they had been separated, both became anxious, and Lightfoot called out with loud meows until Wilde found him and could curl up beside him again.

213593830.description:
Meet Mariska! ❤️

Mariska has been through more than most dogs ever should, but every day she's learning that people can be kind, love can be permanent, and home is a safe place. In 2025, we rescued a litter of her puppies, but we were finally able to rescue her this year. After spending so much of her life surviving and raising babies, this sweet mama is ready to retire, relax, and let someone take care of her for a change.

She's embracing indoor life and making incredible progress. Mariska has discovered the joy of toys and is wonderfully goofy when she plays—leaping, hopping, tossing toys into the air, and catching them herself. She's also incredibly smart! She already knows how to ring the bells to go outside, kennel on cue, sit, leave it, and she's eager to keep learning.

Once Mariska trusts you, she becomes the sweetest little shadow, happily following her favorite person from room to room. A few tasty treats, gentle face scratches, and belly rubs are the fastest way to win her heart. At the end of the day, she's happiest curled up beside you, handing out cuddles and plenty of kisses.

Mariska also enjoys the company of other dogs. She has become friends with every foster dog she's met, but she needs slow, thoughtful introductions and usually takes a day or two to feel comfortable. Because of this, she'd do best in a home that won't expect her to enjoy busy dog parks or daycare settings.

Due to her past, Mariska needs a patient adopter who understands that trust takes time. New people can still be frightening for her, and if she's approached too quickly, she may react out of fear. Her foster family is helping her build confidence, but she'll need someone committed to continuing that journey. For now, she would do best in a home without young children.

When Mariska first entered rescue, she struggled with separation anxiety, barking in her kennel, pawing at the door, or pulling nearby items inside for comfort. She has made tremendous progress, though it's possible some of those behaviors may temporarily return as she adjusts to a new home.

Mariska is looking for someone who will see past her fears and appreciate the incredible dog she's becoming. If you're willing to give her patience, consistency, and unconditional love, she'll reward you with unwavering loyalty, endless affection, and the joy of watching a once-forgotten dog truly blossom into the companion she was always meant to be. ❤️

Lottie does have a high prey drive, so any home with cats would need to have a very dog-savvy, confident cat, and slow, thoughtful introductions would be essential. She may also be happiest in a home without small animals.

After spending years taking care of everyone else, it's finally Lottie's turn to be loved. She's ready for a family who will cherish her, appreciate her loyal heart, laugh at her adorable sideways ear, and give her the forever home she's been waiting for.

Could Lottie be the missing piece of your family?

Toa is the funny little character of the Volcano Crew! This sweet boy has a personality that will keep you smiling. When he gets excited, he hops around like a little frog, and it is absolutely adorable.

Toa has a wonderful mix of playful and affectionate energy. He loves to explore, play, and be part of whatever is happening, but he’s also a sweet, snuggly boy who loves his people. He’s very outgoing and friendly and seems to think everyone he meets is his new best friend.

He also has a particular love of nibbling on toes—which somehow makes the name Krakatoa feel even more fitting!

Toa is doing exceptionally well with potty training and goes potty right away when taken outside. He’s also learning to walk on a leash and practicing his basic commands, including “sit.” He’s a bright little guy and is already showing how eager he is to learn.

Toa is wonderful with kids and other dogs and would make a fantastic addition to a family looking for a happy, affectionate, playful companion with a whole lot of personality.

Meet Kilimanjaro, “Killy”.

Killy is the gentle, thoughtful boy of the Volcano Crew. He’s a little more cautious than his brothers and likes to take his time exploring new surroundings. Once he’s comfortable, though, his sweet and playful personality shines through!

Killy is an absolute snuggle bug. He loves curling up with his people and looking into your eyes with those beautiful blue-gray eyes of his. He’s calm, gentle, loving, and has the sweetest demeanor. He definitely has a playful side, especially when wrestling with his brothers, but he’s also smart enough to know when he needs a little break from their puppy energy.

Killy is doing exceptionally well with potty training and goes potty right away when taken outside. He’s also learning to walk on a leash and practicing his basic commands, including “sit.”

He is wonderful with kids and other dogs and loves being around people. Killy would make an incredibly sweet, loyal, and loving addition to his forever family.

214173138.description:
Hey there! I’m Jasmine!

• My Origin Story: Rescued from under an abandoned shed in Arkansas with my two

brothers.

• My Personality: Sassy, spunky, brave, and completely fearless.

• My Favorite Things: Running outdoors, playing with other dogs, making kid friends, and

getting treats.

From Humble Beginnings to Big Adventures:

My brothers and I started out under an abandoned shed in Arkansas, but I was born to explore! I am the ultimate adventurer. If my brothers are hesitant about going somewhere new, I just charge right right in to show them how it's done. I love the great outdoors and am very good at staying close to my foster parents when I'm off-leash. There is just too much fun stuff to see!

Small Package, Big Personality:

People say I am spunky and sassy. I also have zero problems voicing my thoughts, opinions, and demands—I am highly communicative! I am also completely fearless. If someone or something big comes into "my space," I will absolutely question their existence at first. But don't worry! As soon as I know you, it is nothing but non-stop butt wiggles and sweet puppy kisses.

Smart Girl Status:

I am learning how to be the best dog ever, and I'm progressing fast:

• Potty Training: I am doing amazing! I prefer to go outdoors. When I'm inside, I use my potty

pads like a pro. The only time I have an accident is when I get super tired.

• Basic Commands: I am practicing my manners and learning commands. My absolute

favorite part of school is getting the treats!

My Dream Family:

I absolutely love other dogs and I love kids! My perfect forever home will have plenty of outdoor

playtime, some fun furry or human siblings, and a family who appreciates a brave girl with a lot of look-at-me attitude.

He’s currently a little more string bean than big scary Rottweiler, but don’t let the skinny legs fool you. He’s heartworm positive and will be starting treatment soon, and once that’s behind him, we’re excited to watch him fill out and thrive.

My name’s Dozer! My name has two meanings: For one, I lean in hard for snuggles sort of like a bulldozer.  And two, and I LOVE to doze off on the couch, on a blanket, a pillow, you name it really.  I’ll sleep anywhere.  I love to take long hard naps while my foster family is off at work and school.  I came into rescue the first week of August, and I’ve been an absolute dream for my foster family.  I’m an easy going dude, just so happy for the love and affection of the people around me.  I currently live with three other dogs and two kids, and I’m happy with all of them.  I haven’t played much with dogs or toys just yet; I love human affection the most.  I haven’t had any accidents in the house, and I’ve been a perfect gentleman in the kennel.

I came into rescue with some allergies, making me a little itchy and my hair falling out.  I am starting treatment with the vet, and I’m hoping it’ll start to grow back soon.  Until I have my hair, my humans have to be careful with how long I’m outside in the heat.  Without my fur, I can’t regulate my body temperature very well.

If you are looking for a big dude that loves to lean in for snuggles, take slow meandering walks so I can sniff all the interesting smells, and let me have long naps on the couch, please submit an application so you can learn more about me!

214137637.description:
May is a sweet and affectionate girl who loves to play, demand attention, and snuggle on the couch with you. She loves to play with toys and other dogs, as well as her people! She likes to give kisses, and she won’t be shy asking for attention… if she wants to be pet, she will nuzzle her head underneath your arm to let you know it’s time to give her some loving! Once she’s had her fill, she will curl up next to you and snooze away, snores and all!

She had a few accidents in the house at first, but after an adjustment period she has been great. She is left to free roam during the day and sleeps in a separate room at night without any accidents. She is also starting to walk towards the door if she needs to go out. She goes out on the leash for walks in the yard and around the block and will do her business.

She walks fairly well on the leash, although she does have a bit of a prey drive and will want to go after rabbits/squirrels on walks, but with a little redirection she does well. She has also gotten a little excited around cats, but when she’s had another dog to play with, she has ignored the cats.

Because of this, we think she would thrive in a home with another dog so she has someone to play with and someone to show her the ropes. She would do alright on her own too, but she would definitely love a playmate! She might do better in a home without cats, but could possibly get used to the right cat! She also LOVES to sniff outside looking for things, so she would do well in a home with a fence or safe area to run around in.

Overall, May is a super sweet girl and would make a great fit for the right home who could give her lots of love, attention, and playtime!

214247485.description:
TODAY is the perfect day to find your new best friend. Why not make it a perfect little girl who is so unique and interesting that everyone will stop in their tracks to greet her!? One with a beautiful, thick, (but soft) wire hair coat, the softest ears and chest, a tail that can curl or be held straight, and cute little terrier-inspired chin hairs? Maybe one with built-in mascara eyes and the most expressive eyebrows!?

This puppy is incredible. She is the best of ALL worlds. She is respectful and sweet with other dogs and very gentle and affectionate with all people, including kids.

She is extraordinarily flexible and very good at going with the flow. She likes toys and can entertain herself when her people are busy. She loves to play with other dogs, but also wants to rest afterward and won’t overwhelm them with endless play sessions. She loves to snuggle with her people, and forms bonds immediately. She really enjoys meeting new people. Whoopie rides beautifully in the car and is a professional at dropping off and picking the kids up from school. She sleeps all night in her kennel without a peep. She is wonderful in the shower, and has let me cut her nails and clean her ears without so much as a flinch. Overall, Whoopie is a medium energy dog who just wants to please her people-she would enjoy spending a lot of time with her people. She has a very laid back demeanor. I have to admit-it was love at first sight and has been perfection ever since.

Whoopie is waiting for her forever people to find her. Until then, she will be with us, continuing to work on basic obedience and skills training, potty training, and kennel training, although she is already very well-behaved and doing great with all of these things. She has recently learned to walk on a leash and is doing an amazing job!

Puppies like this one get scooped up quickly! Submit an application for adoption through Rescue Network!

Jimothy is a big, goofy guy with a BIG personality! He’s the kind of dog who will keep you entertained, and make sure you always know exactly what he’s thinking. He loves his toys, has plenty to say, and is happiest when he gets to be part of the action.

After coming from an overcrowded shelter, Jimothy has made huge progress learning that he’s safe and that his people always come back. He’s gone from panicking when someone leaves the room to settling in and relaxing more and more each day.

Jim is still working on his manners and leash skills, but underneath all that goofy energy is a very sweet, silly boy who just wants to be loved. He does well with other dogs when given slow, thoughtful introductions, but he is not a good fit for a home with cats or small animals due to his high prey drive.

Jimothy is looking for someone who will appreciate his big personality, give him a little patience and guidance, and let him continue learning at his own pace. He has come such a long way already, and we know his person is out there!

Could Jimothy be your goofy, lovable guy?

When Bodie came into our home, he was visibly defeated in many ways. Sad droopy eyes, insanely itchy, he couldn’t believe he was able to go outside multiple times a day and defaulted to going into his kennel because that’s all he knew.

It took only a couple days for him to realize he was saved and welcomed into the good life. He is truly the best dog anyone could ask for.

Bodie shares a foster home with 4 other dogs and 6 cats. He gets along with everyone with absolutely no worries. He is kennel trained as he feels safe and comfortable in there. He sleeps through the night peacefully and is completely potty trained. He loves to lay out in the grass and soak up all the sun.

Bodie is such a special guy and deserves the best retirement home. ❤️

My name is Bacon, and before you ask… yes, everyone smiles when they hear my name. I’m a sweet little girl with the cutest white coat covered in black spots, but my foster family will tell you my biggest personality trait is my curiosity. I want to know what you’re doing, where you’re going, and whether I can come too! Every new sound, smell, toy, and adventure is worth investigating.

I’m gentle, affectionate, and absolutely love people, but I also have a playful side. I have no problem romping around with my foster family’s 80+ pound Lab mixes—they may be huge, but I think we’re all the same size when it’s time to play!

I’m also doing a great job learning my potty routine. Every time we go outside, I potty like a good girl! I’m still learning all the puppy basics, but I’m eager to please and catching on quickly.

I might let you know I’d rather not go into my crate with a few puppy protests, but I settle in quickly and snooze like a champ once I’m cozy.

Right now, I’m safe in foster care, but what I really dream about is having a family of my very own. Someone to explore the world with, snuggle up next to after a busy day, and love with my whole little heart.

Maybe I’ve been curious about you all along.

Teddy is estimated to be around 4 years old, although his adorable gray “goggles” make him look like a distinguished elderly gentleman. He’s currently rocking a slightly questionable haircut while recovering from a skin issue, but he’s healing wonderfully and his fur is growing back nicely. Before long, he’ll be back to his handsome, fluffy self!

Teddy loves going for walks and is always ready to explore—especially if there might be a squirrel nearby. He is absolutely obsessed with squirrels and takes squirrel patrol very seriously!

One of the best things about Teddy is how easygoing he is. He does great with dogs, puppies, cats, and kids of all ages. He even enjoys spending time in his kennel, making downtime a breeze.

Teddy is sweet, affectionate, social, and just an all-around great dog. He’s ready to trade his goofy haircut and temporary foster life for a forever home filled with cuddles, belly rubs, walks, and plenty of windows for squirrel watching.

Who’s ready to give this handsome little gentleman the forever family he deserves?

Dash is a loving and loyal tripod. He had his front right leg amputation in April 2026, and he’s adapted quite well. He loves to cuddle with people on the couch.

He enjoys going for walks and resting in the shade outside watching the world. Dash is potty trained and does not mark indoors. He gets along well with the resident female chihuahuas.

While Dash does not prefer the crate, but he will settle down in it. He has done excellent being left unattended or home alone.

214265487.description:
Hi, I’m Oscar!

I’m still figuring out this whole “being a dog” thing.

I came from a difficult situation, and to be honest, the world is a pretty scary place for me right now. People, new places, noises, and unfamiliar things can all feel like a lot. I’m not the kind of dog who is going to run up to you and ask for pets right away. I need time to figure you out, and I need you to give me the time to figure things out.

I’m looking for a quiet, calm home where I can take things at my own pace. A home with adults or older, respectful kids would be best for me. Lots of noise, activity, or being expected to jump right into family life would probably be overwhelming.

I’m still learning that people can be safe and kind. When I’m scared, I may avoid being picked up or handled, and if I get really overwhelmed, I can even have an accident. It’s not because I’m being difficult—I’m just genuinely frightened. The good news is that when I feel safe, those things get better. I’m learning, just very slowly..

I’m also working on my leash skills, and I’m actually doing pretty well! The leash itself doesn’t scare me. It’s everything beyond the front door that I’m still trying to understand. Having a person with me who helps me feel safe makes a big difference, and I’m making little bits of progress every day.

I’m not going to pretend I have everything figured out. I don’t. I’ll need someone who is willing to keep working with me, give me structure and consistency, and understand that my progress probably won’t happen overnight. Some days I may surprise you, and other days I may take a step backward. I’ll need someone who can be patient with both.

What I’m hoping for is pretty simple: a safe home, a patient person, and the chance to learn what it’s like to be loved and cared for. I may not know how to be the dog you’re looking for just yet, but I’m trying.

Maybe, with the right person beside me, I can learn.

214265511.description:
Tito is suspected to have come to us from a hoarding situation after potentially being bred / a "stud." After a difficult start to life, he is understandably guarded and defensive, and he will need a patient, understanding adopter who is willing to let him build trust at his own pace.

Tito is smart, sassy, independent, and incredibly curious. He’s a bit like a “wisp of smoke”—quick, elusive, and determined to keep all four paws on the ground! He isn’t comfortable being picked up yet, but we’re making progress every day.

He has especially begun to trust his foster mom, choosing to curl up beside her in her recliner. Because of this, we suspect Tito may be more comfortable with women and may need extra time to feel safe around men. He is also gradually warming up to his teenage foster grandsons, showing us that his circle of trust can grow with patience and consistency.

Tito appears to have had little-to-no training before coming into rescue. He is currently pee-pad trained and sleeps quite a bit.

For now, Tito is not a fan of other dogs. He reacts strongly toward the resident dog, so they are kept separated. He is also a significant flight risk and has managed to escape harnesses and take off, so his adopter will need to be extremely careful and use secure, escape-proof equipment and management.

Tito is not going to be an “easy” dog, but he is a worthwhile one. His adopter will need to be committed to giving him time, structure, patience, and plenty of opportunities to learn that the world can be a safe place. In return, they’ll get a smart, savvy, energetic little companion.

Tito is looking for someone who understands that trust isn't given overnight—it’s earned one tiny step at a time. And with Tito, those tiny steps are incredibly rewarding.

213961460.description:
Meet Puck! ❤️

If you’re looking for a loyal cuddle buddy, a gentle soul, and a dog who would happily be your copilot on every adventure, Puck might just be your perfect match!

Puck is an incredibly easy companion to welcome into your home. This sweet, affectionate boy is happiest when he’s close to his people, soaking up all the love he can get and giving plenty of kisses in return. While he’s quiet and well-behaved in his kennel, his favorite place is much closer to his humans—preferably curled up beside you on the couch, enjoying some serious cuddle time.

Puck has the most irresistibly big, fluffy, squishy face, and he absolutely LOVES having his cheeks rubbed. ❤️

His foster family has been pleasantly surprised by Puck’s lower energy level, especially considering his breed mix. An Embark DNA test revealed that Puck is an Australian Cattle Dog, Siberian Husky, and German Shepherd mix. Despite those active breeds, Puck isn’t currently interested in running around or playing with the other dogs in his foster home. Instead, you’ll usually find him happily lying near his humans, soaking up their company. He hasn’t shown much interest in toys either, although that may change as he continues to heal, settle in, and gain confidence in his new home.

He is currently living in a foster home with cats. His breed tends to have a higher prey drive and he has shown that, so he would do best in a home without cats.

Puck is still discovering the joys of food and treats and is gradually becoming more food- and bone-motivated. He already knows how to sit and is eager to learn more, especially when it means spending time with his favorite people. Like many happy dogs, he may occasionally jump up when he’s excited to see you, but it’s all out of love.

Say hello to Radley, a handsome boy who is growing into one very special boy. Radley is the kind of pup who simply wants to be where his people are. Whether that means snuggling beside you, following you around the house, or just being able to see his favorite humans, he’s happiest when he’s part of the family.

Radley is cuddly, loyal, and incredibly food-motivated, which makes him eager to learn and a joy to train. But his desire for food means he also counter-surfs. He’s already doing amazing with housetraining and basic commands, and he’s getting more confident and comfortable every day. As his personality comes out more, his playful puppy spirit is really starting to show. He's kid tested and mother approved!

When he’s not busy learning, Radley loves a good Himalayan chew or squeaky toy. He’s also working on becoming comfortable in his kennel and making great progress.

Radley would love a family who will continue helping him learn, give him plenty of love and guidance, and understand that he’s still a puppy with lots of growing to do. He’s going to be a large boy, but underneath those big paws is a pup who just wants to love his people and be loved right back.

Radley is looking for someone who will be his person — his safe place, his adventure buddy, and his forever family.

A few words that describe Radley:

- Cuddly

- Loyal

- Smart & trainable

- People-oriented

- Chew-toy enthusiast

- Food motivated

- Doing great with housetraining

- Coming out of his shell more every day

Could Radley be your next family member? He’s ready to find the people who will love him for all the goofy, sweet, loyal puppy he is — and watch him grow into the incredible dog he’s meant to be.

Admiral loves long walks in quiet parks, but is a bit nervous on busy city streets. Word of warning to the squirrels of the world: Admiral is watching and dreaming of chasing you up a tree.

He is a mellow cuddle bug, happy to get belly rubs any time. He is incredibly gentle when offered food by hand and had shown zero food aggression. He likes to rough-house, which had clearly been an okay form of play in his last home. I personally don't mind it, but would work on training him away from jumping/mouthiness during playtime. He is a very gentle dog, but playtime means rough house time: he does not understand how to play with toys, just yet. I have tried a flirt pole, which gets his attention briefly, but a real fur lure would probably work best. He loves running around in the yard and is a lot of fun to play with, even when he's being a nutter! If you have a fenced in yard, he'll be in heaven!

He is crate trained and has done well with my schedule, which requires him being kenneled up for 9.5 hours on work days. He has been quiet outside and nonreactive to neighbors, dogs, and barriers.

213983707.description:
Opal is a tiny warrior wrapped in the softest, sweetest soul. After spending over a week in the hospital fighting parvo, she beat the odds with quiet determination. Now she’s learning how to enjoy the world again — slowly, softly, and at her own pace.

This mellow little pup wants connection so badly, but eye contact can still feel a bit overwhelming. She’ll peek at you, look away, then try again. Her bravery comes in small, precious steps.

Now that she’s feeling better, Opal has discovered two great joys in life: food and soft squeaky toys. She’s also the cleanest puppy her foster has ever met. While she’s still working on potty training, she does wonderfully with potty pads.

Opal isn’t a fan of baths, but she adores soft, fuzzy pajamas — especially when the air conditioning feels chilly. She’s a comfort‑seeker at heart.

Opal is searching for a patient, gentle home that celebrates tiny victories and understands that courage grows slowly. She may not be fully brave yet, but she’s trying every day, and she’ll blossom beautifully with someone who lets her move at her own pace.

She is happy being held and just cuddles right into your neck.  This girl is so thankful to have a loving home and she shows you how much you mean to her.  It just melts your heart.

Belle is a smaller medium size and petite build.  She LOVES kids and enjoys playing.  She gets along very well with other dogs.  Currently she lives on a hobby farm with chickens, cats, horses, dogs and kids.   She walks right by chickens with no interest in chasing.  She has been very good with the cats.  She is interested in them but doesn't chase.

She is very well behaved and aware of her surroundings.  She is very good about staying away from the horses and moving vehicles (tractors, 4-wheelers).

Belle will make a very lucky family very happy someday soon!!!   This sweet little pup has an ENORMOUS amount of love to give!!

If you looked up “cuddling” in the dictionary, you’d probably find Bean’s picture right there! His soft eyes and sweet little look are enough to make you fold and give him anything he wants. And honestly, he knows exactly how to work those eyes!

Bean is a lovable, medium-energy pup who has mastered the art of giving hugs and cuddles. He is so soft, sweet, and affectionate that once you pick him up, you may have a hard time putting him back down!

Bean is doing well in his crate and is working on his house-training. He is wonderful with other dogs and loves to play. He is also a big fan of treats, which should make training a fun and rewarding experience for this smart boy. He has even done wonderfully with baths and nail trims—pretty impressive for a pup his age!

We could see Bean fitting into just about any setting, from a home with a yard to an apartment, as long as he gets the exercise and attention he needs. An active person would be a great match for him because Bean would make an awesome hiking or trail-walking buddy. With continued socialization, we could even see him becoming your brewery sidekick!

But at the end of the day, Bean is happiest when he is close to his people, soaking up all the love and giving plenty right back.

Does Bean sound like your perfect match? ❤️ This sweet little love bug is ready to find his perfect person—and he’s waiting to give them all the hugs!

I especially love cuddling in a cozy spot and laying my head on my people's lap. I'm doing amazing with kennel and potty training. I'll learn whatever I need to, as long as it means I get to be by your side.

Nos is a timid young adult who is learning to trust people. He takes a bit of time to warm up, but once he has accepted you, he will follow you everywhere. He has attached himself to our 18-year-old son and is thrilled to hang out and snuggle with him.

Once he’s comfortable with you, Nos soaks up the scratches and attention. He loves to nap on the couch, with his head in your lap. He’s even offered a few tentative kisses in the 24 hours we’ve had him.

Nos is just beginning to decompress and gain confidence in life and his environment. He needs people to be slow and patient with him for now. He doesn’t like to feel like he’s being chased or forced to do something - he’d rather think things are his idea. He will go in a crate and hang out a bit, but will bark if you leave him there. He’s happy to explore in our fenced backyard, but it works best if we open the door and let him head out when he’s ready. This will improve in time; he’s had a lot to figure out in a short amount of time.

He’s not yet interested in playing with the other dogs at our house - because they’re not the dogs he’s used to. But he’s been relatively patient with meeting them.

When Nos meets people, he’s more comfortable when they get down to his level (or sit on a couch), rather than tower over him. He will take a slow sniff, then allow you to pet him. After all, he knows he is darling!

Nos is a beautiful boy! He’s got the sweetest chocolate eyes and super soft fur. With time and patience, he will make a great pet!

Mojave is an incredibly nice and sweet dog. He’s super adaptable and settles into new situations with ease.

Mo gets along well with other dogs. He’s happy to run, wrestle and play. But he’s also happy to just chill nearby. He “reads the room” well.

People are also Mojave’s friends. He loves to jump up on a couch or chair to snuggle. He loves a good scratch and gives some loving kisses in return. If you’re lucky, he might even play tug with you!

Don’t let this boy’s eyebrows fool you. He may look a little cranky or suspicious, but he’s actually the friendliest dog in town!

Mo loves his food - and his treats! He wolfs it right down. This will be an advantage when training him because he will do anything for a treat! It does take him a minute to figure out what you’re asking him to do - but he’s brand new to this whole training business.

For the most part, Mojave is potty trained. He’ll probably do best on a schedule for a bit, but he’s had few accidents in the handful of days we’ve had him. He keeps his crate clean, too. He sleeps in his crate, but he will put up a few minutes of protest before accepting that you’re not coming to rescue him. A stuffed Kong sweetens the deal!

Mojave is a rather quiet boy so far. He hasn’t barked yet (even when the resident German Shepherd invites him to scare away squirrels.) He does whine a bit to make his needs known.

This is truly one delightful pup who would do well in so many different households! (We were told when we picked him up that he may not be good with cats, but we haven’t been able to test that.) He’s super flexible, loves everybody and is one of the nicest dogs around!

She walks well on a leash as long as her person is alert for squirrels!!

She loves to sit patiently and watch out the window for squirrels. She is not a barker even with those hound dog ears.

Lorraine would do best with another dog in the family to help her feel safe and show her the ropes, and she would benefit from having a fenced in backyard. She enjoys playing chase with any dog willing to run fast, and she likes to wrestle (very quietly) with the foster family’s cattle dog.

She’s not been around cats or young kids.  Pretty sure she would appreciate the more predictable movements of adolescents.

Lorraine can be quite willful when it comes to going in her crate, or putting on her collar to go for a walk. She’s very food motivated so she would thrive in a beginning level obedience class.

She’s a beautiful dog looking for someone who works from home so she doesn’t have to spend a great deal of time in her crate. She sleeps quietly on her own bed next to her foster parents.

Lorraine has faced a truckload of traumas and daunting challenges in her short life. She’s waiting for the right person or family to envelope her with care, structure, and love to help her become her best self. She’s soooo worth the investment of time and energy!

Tennessee is a sweet, affectionate young pup who is so happy to have a safe place to call home. She has a medium energy level with bursts of puppy enthusiasm and loves playing with toys, spending time with her people, and hanging out with her dog friends. She’s intelligent, eager to learn, and has already shown that she can listen when redirected.

Tennessee is doing well with house training and is currently going potty outside about 90% of the time. Puppy pads by the door help her when she doesn’t quite make it outside. Like many young dogs, she is still working on her manners and can be mouthy and energetic, but she responds well to a firm “no” and will benefit from continued positive training and consistency.

She gets along well with other dogs and would likely love having a young, playful canine companion to help keep her company and burn off some of that puppy energy. She currently sleeps peacefully on a dog bed alongside her foster dog siblings all night.

Tennessee is interested in cats and wants to play with them a little more enthusiastically than they would prefer! With her young age and trainability, she may be able to learn appropriate manners around cats, but a home with dog-savvy cats and a family committed to supervision and training would be best. She has not been tested with young children, so that would be something to consider carefully.

She is still learning that meals are going to keep coming, and she tends to gobble her food as though she might not get another chance. Slow feeding and consistency should help her learn that she is safe and cared for.

Tennessee doesn’t seem to be a flight risk and appears incredibly grateful to have a home and people who care for her. She’s a young dog with plenty to learn, but underneath that puppy energy is a loving, intelligent girl who is going to make someone an absolutely wonderful companion.

Tennessee would thrive with a family who is ready to give her the structure, training, patience, and love she needs to become her very best self.

214354283.description:
Looking for a spunky, energetic kitten?! Cari is your girl!

When she first arrived, she was pretty sick, but after a quick visit to the vet and the necessary meds, Cari was feeling better almost immediately! It wasn't long before her brave, energetic personality really began to shine! You may notice her right eye looks a little different. This is a temporary effect of the severe upper respiratory infection she had when she arrived in our care, but it should resolve on its own now that Cari has finished her meds and is feeling like a healthy kitten again!

Cari is a very playful and social girl. She loves being around people and even better if they are up for a play session! She is obsessed with her crinkle ball, but can make a toy out of literally anything... whether you like it or not :) This includes fingers and toes... but we are working on redirecting her with actual toys when that happens! For this reason, older children may be a better fit for her. She has even found dog toys to be equally as fun as cat toys! Cari has been living with 3 dogs and 3 cats. She LOVES to play with one of our foster dogs. They have become really great friends! She even likes to nap near him. So safe to say she is dog friendly! She has been very hesitant about meeting the resident cats, but with time and proper introductions, I think she could do well with a friendly, playful feline companion.

Cari plays to her heart's content, which also means she works up quite an appetite! Cari is a huge fan of meal time and doesn't appear to be picky! She loves it all! So no fighting with this one when it comes to choosing what's for dinner. That's a huge win in our book! She also does really well with being picked up and carried. And when she wants to be put down, she will certainly let you know with her  big girl meow! Once and awhile, mainly at bedtime, she will curl up and snuggle with us humans for a little bit which is a real treat.

Cari is the perfect mix of sweet & spunky- and will certainly keep you laughing every day with her crazy, playful antics!

Colette is a total sweetheart! She’ll be the first to greet you in the morning, it’s the best way to wake up! She’s also a professional snuggler, she’ll gently scooch over onto your lap and nuzzle her head onto your shoulder.

She gets along wonderfully with every dog she meets. And loves to give kisses to the kids in the house. She’s completely house trained. She does fine in the crate, but she does have a hard time once she hears the front door close, and she’ll whine for about few minutes. She eventually settles though!

Colette has been my one of my husband’s favorite fosters (and we’ve fostered almost 40 dogs!) She’s very calm and gentle, and spends most of her day snoozing on the couch.

She will be getting her left eye removed soon! It’s hazy and she can’t see out of it. Our resident dog has only 1 eye, so I’m pretty fond of 1 eyed dogs!

Denise is a complete sweetheart. She’s just learning to cuddle but follows me from room-to-room all day. She likes to be close to her people. She does great in her kennel at night and frequently naps in it during the day.

She gets along very well with our three large dogs and does not seem intimidated by them. Unless she tests their boundaries with food and then gets put in her place. She is also great with my granddaughters ages 7 and 13. She is fairly vocal especially when she wants to play.

We’re working on potty training and she is doing really well. Now that she figured out the doggie door she goes outside with other dogs and seems to be doing her business outside most of the time. She does get excited, especially when being greeted, and leaks a little sometimes.

All in all for a stray she is very affectionate and a fast learner. I think she will have a sassy personality and be a fairly active dog. We love her already!

214347367.description:
Meet the Salad Litter!

These tiny pups are hard at work mastering their most important jobs: napping, eating, playing, and learning how to be dogs! They’re soft, clumsy little bundles of joy who are already stealing hearts wherever they go.

Their mama, Ambrosia, looks like a German Shepherd, and based on some of the pups’ features, there’s likely a little Husky mixed in too!

The Salad pups love piling on top of each other for meals, playtime, and naps. They’re discovering the joy of chewing on puppy toys, soaking up cuddles from their humans, and giving the sweetest puppy-breath kisses.

These little ones are looking for adopters who understand that puppies take patience, consistency, and lots of love. Their new families should be ready for potty training, teething, basic obedience, and all the adorable chaos that comes with learning how to be a puppy!

Because socialization and potty-training routines are so important at this age, they’ll need homes where they won’t be left alone for long periods of time.

If you’re ready to add one of these sweet salad sprouts to your family, apply to adopt today! Before you know it, one of these little pups could be snuggled right in your arms.

When I’m tired, I like to cuddle and be very sweet. I like toys and puppy chews and a little filled Kong will keep me occupied for a while if you need to leave me. I’m definitely food motivated! I came into rescue with my little brother and we both had non-contagious mange, which has been treated. My coat is still a little patchy right now, but my foster mom tells me I’m going to have the most beautiful glow up! She says I’m pretty just the way I am, but I’m going to be quite beautiful once my fur grows in!  I’m also very smart and I’m doing very well with potty training!  Reach out if you want to meet me!

214550275.description:
Meet Cole!

It’s hard to believe that this sweet soul spent FOUR YEARS in a Georgia shelter after being surrendered by his owners at just two years old. Somehow, Cole kept waiting, hoping someone would finally see what we see in him. He even traveled a long way and flew on an airplane to get his second chance and escape being euthanized. And now, at 6-years-old, he is finally ready for the family he should have had all along.

Cole is quite possibly one of the sweetest, gentlest dogs you’ll ever meet. He is an absolute cuddle bug who loves to hug, give kisses, and be as close to his person as possible. He is a true Velcro dog — if you’re moving around the house, he wants to be right there with you. If you sit down, he wants to be beside you. He simply wants to be near his people.

And Cole LOVES children! He is gentle, affectionate, and respectful with kids and genuinely enjoys being around them. He also gets along wonderfully with other dogs, making him a wonderful potential addition to a family with furry siblings.

Cole is fantastic when meeting new people. He is respectful, calm, and friendly, and he has such a gentle demeanor. He also takes treats so delicately — truly one of the gentlest treat-takers! He isn’t a food beggar and is actually a light eater, so he doesn’t need a lot of food to be happy.

He is wonderful on a leash and walks beautifully without pulling. We’re currently working on stairs because they are completely new to him, which is just another reminder of how much he missed out on during those four years.

Cole does not potty in the house, and we’re working through a little marking behavior. Given that he is in a brand-new environment surrounded by unfamiliar smells from other dogs, this is very understandable and something we’re working on with him.

What Cole needs now is someone who will show him that all those years of waiting were worth it. He deserves a soft bed, a loving family, endless cuddles, and a person who will never give up on him.

After everything he has been through, Cole still chooses to be gentle, loving, trusting, and affectionate. He waited four years in a shelter, traveled a long way, flew on an airplane, and survived being overlooked — and somehow, he still has nothing but love to give.

214490493.description:
Meet Fresca! Sweet, shy, and slowly discovering just how wonderful life can be, Fresca is ready to find a family of her very own!

Fresca came into rescue after raising a litter of puppies, and now it’s finally her turn to be the baby! She can be a little nervous and unsure when she first meets people or enters a new environment, but once she realizes she’s safe, her personality starts to shine. Give her a little time, patience, and some gentle encouragement, and you’ll see her come out of her shell more and more each day.

One of Fresca’s favorite recent discoveries? Playing with her foster dog sibling! She has really started to loosen up and enjoys romping and having fun with her resident dog. A friendly, patient dog in her forever home could be a wonderful companion for her, but is not required.

Fresca is also a pretty quiet girl. She doesn't bark when someone comes to the door, which is a nice bonus! Every now and then, though, she likes to remind everyone that she has a voice by letting out a dramatic little howl—usually when she’s unhappy about something. Think of it as her way of filing a formal complaint.

She's making great progress with potty training! While we wouldn't call her fully potty trained just yet, she's had very few accidents since her first couple of days in foster care and is catching on beautifully. She also enjoys her kennel and sleeps there peacefully at night. We're still working on getting her to go into her kennel on command, but she's making progress.

And don't let her shy personality fool you—once Fresca trusts you, she is incredibly affectionate. She loves being close to her people and has a very sweet, loving side that comes out once she feels comfortable.

She's also a surprisingly good little walking buddy! Fresca walks nicely on a leash and doesn't really pull, making her a pleasure to take along on adventures.

Fresca's ideal family will understand that she may need a little time to adjust and won't expect her to become their best friend on day one. Her ideal home will be a calmer home with older kids. She needs people who are willing to give her patience, reassurance, and time to trust.  In return, you'll get to watch an incredibly rewarding transformation as this once-scared mama discovers confidence, playfulness, and the joy of being someone's beloved dog.

Fresca has spent her time taking care of everyone else. Now she's ready for someone to take care of her.

Fresca at a glance:

•	Former mama who is ready to be someone's baby

•	Shy at first, but very affectionate once she trusts you

•	Enjoys playing with other dogs

•	Quiet overall; doesn't bark at the door

•	Occasionally howls when she's displeased

•	Making excellent progress with potty training

•	Sleeps happily in her kennel at night

•	Walks surprisingly well on leash with very little pulling

•	Needs a patient family willing to give her time to settle in

•	Coming out of her shell more every day!

If you're looking for a gentle girl whose trust will feel like something truly special to earn, Fresca might just be your girl.

Joel exhibits some classic German Shepherd traits too, including the occasional land shark behavior, so experience with that breed would be helpful.

If you are looking for a best buddy to explore with, Joel could be the perfect dog for you!

214515534.description:
If you’re looking for a puppy who is equal parts silly, playful, snuggly, and ridiculously cute, allow us to introduce you to Atlantic!

Atlantic has already been through quite a lot. She came into rescue as a stray with a brother, and both were battling both Parvo and Kennel Cough. Sadly, her brother didn't survive. But this little girl is a fighter! She has recovered beautifully in her foster home and is now making up for lost time by filling every day with puppy zoomies, toys, cuddles, and plenty of love.

Atlantic is a total steal-your-heart, social butterfly kind of girl. She loves to play with toys, enjoys hanging out with her foster family, and has four resident doggy foster siblings to keep her company. They come in all different ages and sizes, and Atlantic gets along wonderfully with everyone!

She’s also learning that being a good puppy comes with some pretty great perks. She already knows how to sit for a treat, and she is discovering that going potty outside = TREATS! Since her battle with Parvo meant she couldn’t safely begin outdoor potty training until recently, she has been using potty pads and is kennel trained. Her foster family has just started working with her on the dog door, and she is starting to catch on to this whole “outside is the bathroom” concept.

At bedtime, Atlantic sleeps all night in her kennel right next to foster mom’s bed like a very good girl. During the day, though? She is more than happy to climb next to somebody on the couch, curl up in a dog bed, or snuggle at somebody's feet for a "between zoomies" nap and quality time with her favorite people.

Atlantic is still very much a puppy, so her new family should be prepared for the usual puppy adventures... continued potty training, chewing the right things, learning, playing, and discovering the world. But if you’re ready to help a sweet little girl continue growing into the amazing dog she’s destined to be, Attie would love to meet you.

Silly. Playful. Snuggly. Resilient. Adorable.

That’s our Atlantic with the beautiful eyes. And we have a feeling she’s going to steal someone’s heart very, very soon.

Threesa was brought to an overcrowded shelter in Georgia with a mangled leg that left her in a lot of pain. Her leg got amputated but that didn’t slow her down.

Threesa is truly one of the most loving, affectionate kittens you’ll ever meet. She purrs LOUD, makes biscuits like it’s her full-time job, and wants nothing more than to be snuggled up as close to her person as possible. Her favorite place in the entire world is perched on your shoulder or curled up against your chest. 💕

And don’t let the missing leg fool you. Threesa still LOVES to play! She’s figured out her own adorable way of getting around and tends to bounce like a little bunny instead of running. 🐰

She’s sweet, silly, playful, incredibly cuddly, and completely unfazed by life on three legs.

Threesa lost a leg, but she certainly didn’t lose her sparkle. ✨

If you’re looking for a kitten who will fill your lap with snuggles, your shirt with biscuits, and your house with the sound of one very enthusiastic purr motor, Threesa is your girl. 🩷

214347362.description:
Mama Ambrosia is the proud mom of the adorable “Salad Mix” puppies, and her foster family has lovingly called her “Mom". After spending her time raising, loving, and protecting her  nine babies, this sweet girl is finally ready for something she’s never truly had: a forever family of her very own.

Ambrosia is a loving, loyal girl with a big personality and an even bigger heart. She absolutely loves carrying around her favorite toys and soaking up affection. She’s also incredibly smart! In just the few short weeks she’s been in rescue, she has already learned sit, drop it, outside, and shake. She’s eager to learn and continues to make amazing progress every day.

Like any good mama, Ambrosia can be very protective of what she considers valuable. She has some food reactivity and can occasionally become barrier-aggressive when she has food or high-value treats. She has come a long way in just a few weeks, though, and her progress has been wonderful to watch. When she first arrived, she also showed some toy guarding, but she has not demonstrated that behavior recently.

Ambrosia likely could do well with respectful children given her sweet and affectionate personality, but she has not yet been formally tested with kids, so any introductions would need to be thoughtful and supervised.

After giving her puppies the love, protection, and guidance they needed, she deserves the chance to be someone's baby now. She’s ready for a family who will continue to help her grow, celebrate her progress, and show her just how wonderful life can be.

If you're looking for a loyal companion, a smart girl with plenty of personality, and a best friend who has a whole lot of love left to give, Ambrosia is ready to meet you.

Gelato may be petite, but she has an enormous heart and so much love to give. This happy-go-lucky girl is affectionate, playful, and happiest when she’s surrounded by her people.

Gelato absolutely loves people and kids and has never met a stranger she didn’t want to be friends with. She also does wonderfully with other dogs and is good with cats, making her a wonderful addition to a variety of families.

She’s the kind of dog who is always ready for whatever fun comes next—whether that’s going for a walk, playing, getting cuddles on the couch, or simply hanging out with her family. She loves being included and has a wonderful, easygoing personality.

And this fluffy girl is as sweet as she is adorable! Gelato is potty trained, kennel trained, and a dream for grooming. Baths and brushing? No problem!

Gelato has already shown just how resilient she is, and today she is thriving. She does need a daily B12 supplement to keep her healthy, which costs only about 70 cents a day—an easy little addition for a girl who gives so much love in return.

Gelato is small in size but absolutely HUGE in personality. She’s ready to fill a home with laughter, cuddles, and unconditional love. All she needs now is someone to make her forever.

211013418.description:
INTRODUCING YUKI! This sweet girl is looking for a family, and is hoping it is you!

Yuki is a gentle, good-natured and smart girl. She is potty trained. In her previous home she learned to ring a bell when she wanted to go outside. She is kennel trained, but definitely prefers to be right by your side. She is the best friend you always wanted.

Yuki can be skittish in a new environment, therefore she would love a patient family that will allow her to get comfortable at her own pace. A calm and predictable home with kids 12 and up would be best for her. Chaos can be to overwhelming to her.

Her ideal home would include the following:

Walking and squeaky tennis balls are an absolute must! She is an enthusiastic walker! She pulls a bit to begin with. She wants to get all the smells in, but she will settle down after a short time. Chasing and squeaking her tennis ball is a favorite pastime.

A fenced yard to chase that ball and show off her zoomies.

Yuki really enjoys chasing the cats. While she hasn’t been allowed to get very close to them, living with cats may not be a successful fit.

Calmer dogs only. Yuki does not enjoy dogs that get in her face. If there is another dog in your home, it would need to be a more laid-back pup. She will need a slow, safe introduction to her new sibling.

A window to observe the outside world. She likes to lay in the sun and see the goings on in the neighborhood.

Though she has her playful and adventurous side, sitting beside you on the couch is her favorite way to wrap up the day. If you are a looking for the ultimate companion Yuki is your girl. She is excited to meet you!
